title: Plan in Sandbox, Navigate in Open Worlds: Learning Physics-Grounded Abstracted Experience for Embodied Navigation
claim: A sandbox-trained agent passes through three linked phases to reach open-world deployment, and it beats RL and VLM baselines.
layout: 3 panels: wide pipeline left, photo and bar chart stacked right; sandbox-to-open-world arrow
description: The figure has three panels. Panel (a), on the left and about two-thirds of the width, shows the SAGE agent as three pastel columns: blue GENESIS, orange EVOLUTION and green NAVIGATION. Genesis shows an isometric room, cartoon professor icons, a task document, and a question and answer bubble about a red chair. Evolution shows hybrid sampling with and without experience, augmented samples, and a policy model robot that outputs an optimized policy. Navigation shows a user's question, a top-down simulator map with frontier and memory nodes, a humanoid robot, and visual buffers. A long arrow underneath runs from Sandbox to Open-world. Panel (b), at top right, shows real-world robot photographs with egocentric views. Panel (c), at bottom right, is a grouped bar chart of SR and SPL on GOAT-Bench. It compares RL and VLM paradigms, and the dark blue Ours bar is the tallest.
caption: (a): Our SAGE framework utilizes a physics-grounded sandbox for self-evolving data generation and policy optimization, enabling the agent to bridge the gap between sandbox and open-world. (b): We demonstrate real-world robotic demonstrations powered by SAGE, showcasing its Sim2Real generalization capabilities. (c): Unlike other VLM or RL paradigms, our approach uniquely combines physics-grounded interactions with real-world transfer, demonstrating superior performance in navigation metrics.
abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated exceptional general reasoning capabilities. However, their performance in embodied navigation remains hindered by a scarcity of aligned open-world vision and robot control data. Despite simulators providing a cost-effective alternative for data collection, the inherent reliance on photorealistic simulations often limits the transferability of learned policies. To this end, we propose \textit{\textbf{S}andbox-\textbf{A}bstracted \textbf{G}rounded \textbf{E}xperience} (\textbf{\textit{SAGE}}), a framework that enables agents to learn within a physics-grounded semantic abstraction rather than a photorealistic simulation, mimicking the human capacity for mental simulation where plans are rehearsed in simplified physics abstractions before execution. \textit{SAGE} system operates via three synergistic phases: (1) \textit{Genesis}: constructing diverse, physics-constrained semantic environments to bootstrap experience; (2) \textit{Evolution}: distilling experiences through Reinforcement Learning (RL), utilizing a novel asymmetric adaptive clipping mechanism to stabilize updates; (3) \textit{Navigation}: bridging the abstract policy to open-world control. We demonstrate that \textit{SAGE} significantly improves planner-assisted embodied navigation, achieving a 53.21\% LLM-Match Success Rate on A-EQA (+9.7\% over baseline), while showing encouraging transfer to physical indoor robot deployment.
